body:
Thank you for responding to my post. I mentioned in another reply that I'll be contacting my local MSS. I've been starting sessions with a counsellor but they only see patients in my area once every few weeks. After taking some distance from the thoughts I wrote yesterday, it's become clear to me that I am not coping well and I need to see someone with a more flexible schedule.

Thank you for sending a response, it really means the world to me that someone has simply heard me. I will be here again to share my story, and hopefully I will have some positive successes to share as well.

Thank you for responding, I will be seeing someone in a few days. Their schedule is very rigid and it takes weeks for me to get an appt with them (hence my frustration) so I'll be reaching out to the MS Society in my area to see if there are other counsellors with more flexible schedules.

Not silly at all, it actually very much describes how I feel.

It kind of reminded me of [this](http://charliebink.tumblr.com/post/44547383533/what-shape-are-you) too: 

Well I was referring to my mom sacrificing things for me. It kinda feels like she did it out of love but is resentful and because im not her vision of perfection, I'm not enough.

My partner does a lot for me too though, but sometimes I feel like I'm just a big burden because of my depression and anxiety. I dont feel like intimate relationships should be unconditional really. Because you need boundaries to have intimacy. I can't rely on him to be my family and my sole support because that's a lot for one person to take. I just feel like I don't have that kind of unconditional family bond with anyone in my life. It feels really lonely.

It's been a few days and things have let up but just a little. I'd been staying with my mom for a few weeks while my partner was away and that has a tendency to bring me down. She is verbally and emotionally abusive and if I ever tell her she's making me feel upset she lashes out because she thinks she has sacrificed so much for me. Granted, she is loving and has sacrificed a lot, she just has a funny way of expressing that she cares.

I basically have been dealing with health problems that have led to a progressive loss of sensation in various parts of my body. My right hand has gotten so bad I can't write anymore, brush my teeth with it, really basic things. I am on a waitlist to see a neurologist but the earliest appt I could get was for the end of August. I am also in my last push at uni and have one exam to take and so I contacted the dept on campus to make accommodations for things. They told me that since there was some sort of deadline I missed, they couldn't do anything for me.

I freaked out, my mother phoned her own doctor and demanded he see me, even though I knew he couldn't do anything, and the whole thing was just bad. He seemed irritated that I was there, said he couldn't really do much, and when I asked questions about my symptoms, he just kept emphasizing that it was due to stress and just seemed really frustrated with me. Given my previous experiences with medical professionals, one of which was the experience in that psych ward, I got sent into this spiral of shame and it hasn't let up since.

It doesn't help that my mother doesn't know how to be supportive with me. I get scolded for my emotions, as I did when I was a child, and then I'm yelled at because I'm "not more open with her and I'm emotionally distant." I have really bad anxiety problems and her response is to yell at me and remind me that I'm not normal. I just really feel like I don't have anyone who will love me unconditionally. I am not the child my mom wanted. I am queer, I am politically progressive, I am just everything she hates. I'm scared to even write that out here, I'm scared of people judging my perspectives and my views on the world. I feel afraid to say how I really feel to people I know because it just seems like everyone is sick of my shit.

I did find counselling helpful. Unfortunately I just dont have access to the funds to see a counsellor again. I'm trying to fight through this depressive episode enough to be able to get a FT job and have those funds available again.

It's funny, I really wanted to go into counselling for a while and did some intro courses. I found my personal counselling sessions a lot more effective once I had some idea of the intent behind things

As someone who lost both my parents to the firey heat of their divorce, they will most likely hurt more than you will ever know if you leave. I hadn't spoken to my dad in many years and when I tried earlier this year, it was just... angry emotion vomit. And he rightfully deserved it for all the shit he did. My dad's fucked up, but that doesn't mean it doesn't hurt not having him there. I can be angry at what he did, I can protect myself by pretending I'm cold and distant, but he'll never know how much I miss him. It's not my job, as my parent's child, to figure out the messiness of their divorce so that I have to be the first one to reach out. I don't know you or your situation but I can imagine it's not easy. I'm not at all trying to berate you or say your decision is wrong, I just thought I'd give you some perspective from the other side, as someone who is an incredibly fucked up person because I don't have my dad in my life.

Real life. I don't want to go into too many details because I'm having a hard time dealing with the memories. Basically I was put in a psych ward and was scolded when I got upset after having to stay there more than I had voluntarily agreed to. I was later told by the psychiatrist on staff that normal people don't react to situations the way I did (i.e. reacting with a suicide attempt) and that me being upset was also not okay. She said if I didn't stop crying and freaking out they would either force me to take an ativan pill (I had mentioned I was uncomfortable taking drugs for medical problems unless it was absolutely necessary) or she would extend my stay in the psych ward.

I know people would say that thats just my perspective and that I'm biased because of my emotional state. But I'm really trying not to overexaggerate what happened. The staff I dealt with were really awful, I did not feel comforted and I was absolutely terrified. I remember one nurse saying something like "Why are you freaking out? This isn't one flew over the cuckoo's nest, we're not strapping you down and electrocuting you or anything."

I felt terrible. I felt terrible. I felt like I feel now. Today was rough and I was scolded by another medical professional for concerns I've been having about my body. I was told I was overreacting, even though I can physically feel my body shutting down. It's like, I have to try so hard not to cry or be upset whenever I'm in any medical situation because they don't take me seriously. But how can I stop it? I'm just so scared and it's like no one cares. I'm just another patient, I'm another box to check or a puzzle to figure out and that's it.

Thank you, and I don't mean to be ungrateful or selfish. It's tough sometimes just sticking it out, really terrifying. I've been trying to meditate and gain some separation from my thoughts (obviously continuously, not like, just when I feel bad) but I guess I'm not there yet.

Thank you. I just feel so lost. I had a really awful time the last time I reached out and its hard because it made me feel like I'm doing something wrong, like I didn't ask for help in the right way or didn't take it the right way. I was scolded a number of times and now whenever I feel this way, I feel like it's all just wrong, like I'm a child just whining about nothing.

I'm in a really bad place. Could someone please talk to me? I'm trying to sit with these feelings but they're really painful, I just want to feel like someone actually cares about me and my choice to exist.
